title: It Looks Like John Mayer Is Gearing Up For a Smoldering Cuffing Season: ‘I’ll Run Away With You’
summary: The singer/guitarist has piqued interest with a provocative tease featuring a video in which he is, literally, handcuffed to an unseen woman.
body: It’s been five years since John Mayer released his eighth studio album, 2021’s 1980s inspired Sob Rock . But from the sounds of it, he hasn’t quite escaped the gravity of that decade’s music quite yet. On Thursday (Oct. 15), Mayer, 49, posted a provocative short clip on his Instagram hinting at a new song that might just help kick off the annual cold-weather temporary dating period known as “cuffing season.” Hell, the brief clip literally features what looks like Mayer handcuffed to an unseen woman in a leather jacket and jeans, with the pair subtly, sweetly, linking their pinkies at the end. The post’s caption hints at some upcoming music, teasing, “I’ll run away with you… October 23.” The accompanying soundtrack features a shuffling beat and synth pattern fans noted was similar to Bruce Springsteen’s smoldering 1985 Born in the U.S.A. track “I’m on Fire,” with a snippet of Mayer’s signature blues-based guitar picking coming in at the tail end. At press time Mayer had not provided any additional information about what he has in store. He hinted in August that he’d recently finish…

title: Jacqie Rivera Breaks Down 5 Essential Songs From Her New Album, ‘Corazón Desnudo’: ‘A Very Healing Process’
summary: Jenni Rivera’s eldest daughter talks with Billboard Español about the creative process of her latest album.
body: Jacqie Rivera , the second daughter of iconic regional Mexican singer Jenni Rivera , releases her new album Corazón Desnudo Friday (Oct. 16) via Soundflower Inc/Virgin Music Group. The 12-track collection blends pop-rock with touches of regional Mexican music. “Even though it leans into a different genre, I had to add some of what’s in my DNA,” Rivera tells Billboard Español about her second studio album, following 2025’s En Otra Vida . While juggling her responsibilities as CEO of Jenni Rivera Enterprises — the company that manages her late mother’s legacy and music catalog — Jacqie made time to write some of the songs on her new LP as a form of catharsis. “It was a very healing process,” she says. “It’s not just an album of songs; it’s something I’ve lived through over the past few years. It reflects the things that have brought me to this point in my life.” At a time when music allows for more genre-blending than ever, Rivera experiments with R&B, pop and Latin sounds, channeling emotion through her soft yet powerful voice on songs like “Mi superpoder,” “Pa’ migajas,” “Amaneció en París,” “Rota” and “Cuando cambies volveré.” Corazón Desnudo also includes a particularly mean…

summary: Thought 185Hz was impressive? OnePlus might be thinking about a 240Hz display for the OnePlus 17.
body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR OnePlus is apparently testing a 240Hz refresh rate on the OnePlus 17. title: Android Auto’s missing signal bars are finally making a proper comeback
summary: A wider rollout is restoring the vanished cell network connectivity icon to in-car displays.
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Google is expanding the rollout of a fix that restores the missing network signal icon in Android Auto. The issue began months ago when an update removed the icon, leaving drivers unable to view cell reception status on their car screens. The fix seems to rely on a mix of app updates and server-side flags, so a full rollout across all devices may still take weeks. If you have been driving blind to your phone’s cellular connectivity, relief is finally rolling out. Google appears to be widening the rollout of a fix that restores the missing network signal icon in Android Auto , addressing a frustrating bug that left drivers guessing whether their phone actually had reception. Over the past few days, multiple users on Reddit have reported that the network icon is back on their in-car displays, as mysteriously as it disappeared in the first place. Drivers with different vehicle infotainment setups and phone models are seeing the familiar status indicator rejoin the battery and Wi-Fi icons in the status bar.

title: The Galaxy S27 Plus could break nearly six years of tradition with this downgrade
summary: The potential downgrade reaches beyond finding your misplaced keys.
body: TL;DR Chinese regulatory filings suggest the Galaxy S27 Plus could drop UWB, a feature Plus models have offered since the S21 Plus. That could mean losing more precise tracking and hands-free access to compatible cars and smart locks, although some alternatives would remain. The apparent Pro and Ultra listings include UWB, but Samsung hasn’t confirmed the lineup’s final specifications. Samsung gave its phones a useful sense of direction when it introduced ultra-wideband (UWB) on the Galaxy Note 20 Ultra. The technology promised easier ways to find belongings and the ability to unlock compatible cars without reaching for your phone. Now, the Galaxy S27 Plus could lose that hardware, breaking a streak that began with the S21 Plus. According to leaker Abhishek Yadav on X , Chinese MIIT certifications list UWB for the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra, but omit it from the Galaxy S27 and S27 Plus. That would be business as usual for the base model, since Samsung has consistently left UWB out of its standard Galaxy S phones. It would, however, mark an unexpected downgrade for the Plus after years of support. But these filings don’t establish Samsung’s final global specifications, so the rem…

title: Your next ePaper tablet will feel a lot more colorful, lot less like a faded newspaper
summary: E Ink's new Kaleido 4 displays are far more saturated, offer better visibility, and allow smoother page turning than ever.
body: Credit: E Ink TL;DR E Ink just announced its new Kaleido 4 display technology with support for a wider color gamut. In addition to the colors, the new display offers 50% better contrast. Hanvon Technology’s M10C II is the first ePaper tablet with this display. E Ink’s Kaleido line is considered the gold standard for colored ePaper displays . Kaleido displays are found on leading e-readers from brands such as Amazon, BOOX, Kobo, and others. Building on this, E Ink has now launched Kaleido 4 with richer color, snappier page refreshes, and display quality that leads to a “more detailed and fluid ePaper experience.” In its press note, E Ink says the new Kaleido 4 displays are now suitable for a wider variety of digital content. According to the announcement, the latest version supports a color gamut twice as large, with a volume exceeding 40,000. That does not mean 40,000 colors, but without a unit associated, it’s difficult to make objective sense of the number than just saying that the display will now deliver more saturated colors than before.

title: I wouldn’t buy these phones, and neither should you
summary: There are five phones I wouldn't touch for specific reasons.
body: I’m the Shallow Hal of Android fandom. I wouldn’t touch certain Android phones with a ten-foot pole if they have a specific trait I don’t like. I’m not talking about smartphones with overwhelmingly negative reviews . In fact, there are a few poorly reviewed products I take a fancy to . I’m referring to smartphones that have one or two deal-breakers, in spite of their positive first impressions. It could be as trivial as a missing feature, or more unforgivable like a substantial price hike. Whichever it may be, I’d rather save my money for something else.

title: I ignored this Google Maps feature for 10 years, and now I can’t live without it
summary: No more digging through messages for forgotten addresses.
body: As a person with no sense of direction, I’ve been using Google Maps to get around since the app was first available for my smartphone. Even when I can’t mount my phone to my car dashboard, I use its audio navigation to guide me to destinations I’m not familiar with. But as the app has rolled out newer features, I’ve had a habit of ignoring them. My You tab remains neglected, and I’ve only ever left two reviews (both seven years ago) in the app. I also happily ignore the recommendations that appear when I’m about to search for something. However, recently I decided to revisit the lists and labeled places features — and realized that I’ve been missing out.

body: As weeks go, it was a “pretty weird” one for Powderfinger . In the best possible way. The 18 coast-to-coast concerts that were initially announced for September and October 2027, quickly grew to 26 with dates extending into November. “All shows are expected to sell out,” the statement continues. “With so many fans still hoping to join the biggest singalong of 2027, the band and tour partners are working feverishly on adding more shows,” the band insists. “Fans can be assured that additional shows will be added, one way or another. Details will be shared as soon as they are confirmed.” After a glittering career that produced five consecutive ARIA No. 1 albums, 18 ARIA Awards and three APRA Awards, including a brace for song of the year, Powderfinger called time in 2010 with  The Sunset…

body: I tested Google’s first smart home controller designed for the Gemini era, the Google Home Speaker , more than three months ago. I hoped the Home Speaker would usher in a new wave of Google smart home products, but the opposite has happened in the time since. The Nest Audio and Nest Mini were discontinued, and the second-generation Nest Hub and the Nest Hub Max are both out of stock on the Google Store. title: Sony just proved that ‘three OS updates’ doesn’t really mean anything
summary: Sony needs to offer a much stronger explanation for this.
body: TL;DR Sony has decided not to roll out the Android 17 update to the Xperia 10 VI. The company says it’s due to “technical limitations” of the Xperia 10 VI’s storage configuration. The Xperia 10 VI was promised three OS updates at launch, implying that it would be upgraded to Android 17. Sony started rolling out Android 17 to its flagship Xperia 1 VIII early last month. At the same time, the company released a list of phones eligible for the update, which surprisingly did not include the Xperia 10 VI. While that raised doubts about Sony’s plans for the phone, we now know that it’s simply never getting Android 17 . In a notice posted on its website, Sony confirmed that the Xperia 10 VI, released in 2024, will not be updated to Android 17. According to the company, “technical limitations due to the device’s storage configuration” prevent it from offering an Android 17 experience that Sony considers adequate.

title: Google reminds Android users of an overlooked scam detection tool
summary: Circle to Search and Google Lens can also help you detect scams!
body: TL;DR Google is highlighting Circle to Search’s existing ability to identify suspicious text messages using AI Overviews. We tested the functionality, and it works as intended, with Google explaining why a message might be fraudulent and suggesting next steps. Google Lens offers the same scam-checking functionality on phones without Circle to Search, including iPhones. Google’s suite of scam detection features is great at filtering out suspicious messages and calls before you fall for them. The tech giant has been steadily improving the collection and rolling it out to more users, though that’s also the big catch here. Not all scam detection features are available on every Android phone. Newer developments, like enhanced protection mode in Google Messages , are available on even fewer devices. With the company announcing new tools, it’s worth revisiting an existing one that’s available to a much wider range of users and devices. Google is highlighting that scam detection is available via Circle to Search (CtS) , giving a larger subset of users who don’t have scam detection natively access to preventive tools that can help them avoid falling victim to fraud.

title: ANBERNIC is quietly removing a controversial extra from its Android handhelds
summary: The company is dropping microSD card bundle options just days after facing accusations of distributing pirated games.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR ANBERNIC has started removing optional microSD card bundles from several handheld listings on its official store. The changes follow an ESA complaint accusing ANBERNIC of selling devices bundled with unauthorized games. ANBERNIC hasn’t confirmed a connection, but the move may be intended to head off further action against the company. ANBERNIC has had quite a week. After recently unveiling its Nintendo 3DS-inspired RG DDS handheld — whose potential pricing was leaked earlier today — the company found itself facing scrutiny over the copyrighted games allegedly bundled with its devices. Within days of the complaint coming to light, ANBERNIC now appears to be quietly removing the contentious microSD card options from its online store. As spotted by Retro Handhelds , several ANBERNIC handheld listings have lost the option to purchase additional microSD cards alongside the devices. The publication compared an archived version of the RG SP listing from August 14 with the current storefront, finding that only the 16GB option remains. That card is still needed because it contains the handheld’s stock firmware.

title: Apple might just be Samsung’s best foldable salesperson yet
summary: Samsung just got a free marketing boost.
body: TL;DR Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 series is seeing strong demand, exceeding the company’s initial sales expectations. Samsung says demand for its latest foldables is up 16% since launch, while Google searches for Samsung foldables have surged 300% over the past month. Apple’s entry into the foldable market with the iPhone Duo could be driving more consumers to explore Samsung’s alternatives. There’s no denying that Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 series is having its moment. The South Korean tech giant’s decision to split the book-style segment into two — regular and widescreen — seems to be paying off. We reported that despite an overall decline in global smartphone shipments, strong demand for the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series has softened the blow for Samsung, and while the credit does go to Samsung for refining its lineup, there also appear to be some outside forces at play. Interestingly, one of those outside forces is Samsung’s biggest rival.

Android’s built-in earthquake alerts are expanding to a lot more places. Google’s announced that the system that’s been available in 98 countries and regions to date is now available in more than 200. The alerts themselves are getting an upgrade, too. title: Is your Pixel recording unusually quiet audio? You’re not alone
summary: Still dealing with microphone issues first reported back in 2024.
body: TL;DR Several Pixel owners are reporting unusually low microphone volume when recording audio/video natively or via certain apps. Similar complaints date back to 2024 and span multiple Pixel generations, including the latest Pixel 10 series. Google appears to be aware of the complaints but hasn’t publicly acknowledged a widespread issue, and there’s no confirmed fix yet. Apart from offering one of the best software experiences in the Android smartphone ecosystem, Google’s Pixel line is also known for its impressive camera capabilities . However, what good is a high-res video recording if you can barely hear anything when you play it back? That’s exactly the frustration that a lot of Pixel owners are (and have been) dealing with. This isn’t a brand new issue, but it is resurfacing now. Reports about Pixel microphones recording audio that’s too quiet to hear can be traced back to 2024, and similar microphone problems appear to have continued to plague users since.

title: Qualcomm’s lengthy legal battle with Arm nets it $2 (not a typo) in damages
summary: Two dollars today, potentially billions tomorrow.
body: TL;DR A Delaware jury has awarded Qualcomm $2 in damages in its legal fight with Arm. The jury sided with Qualcomm on two counts, and with Arm on five counts. The legal battle will now go to a US federal judge who will resolve several other issues. Qualcomm and Arm have been involved in a series of legal battles over several issues over the last couple of years. Since Qualcomm acquired Nuvia back in 2021, Arm has threatened to cancel Qualcomm’s architecture licensing agreement (ALA), and Qualcomm has filed lawsuits against Arm. According to a Reuters report, the verdict is finally in for Qualcomm’s latest lawsuit against Arm. The Delaware jury has sided with Qualcomm on two counts, awarding it damages amounting to $2. Yes, that’s not a typo.

title: Samsung Galaxy phones can’t tell if they’re connected to Bluetooth or not
summary: The Samsung Galaxy's volume slider is mixing up its connected device icons.
body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung Galaxy phone users are experiencing a strange bug affecting the volume panel. When playing audio through the phone’s speakers, a Bluetooth icon appears at the bottom of the slider. Instead of an earbud icon, a speaker icon reportedly appears when earbuds are connected. You may not always notice it, but the volume slider on your Galaxy phone conveys more information than just the volume level. Whether you’re listening to music through your earbuds or blasting it through your Bluetooth speakers, there will be a little symbol at the bottom of the panel that lets you know what your phone is connected to. However, a new bug is causing issues with this indicator. Samsung Galaxy phone users ( 1 , 2 , 3 ) are experiencing a strange glitch affecting the volume panel. When playing audio through the handset’s speakers, a Bluetooth icon appears at the bottom of the slider. That should not be happening, as it suggests the phone is connected to a Bluetooth device even though it is disconnected. Users also report seeing a speaker icon instead of an earbud icon when their earbuds are connected.

The issue seems like it might be limited to the Pixel 10 series. Google is aware of the problem and is investigating it. For a phone that’s at the forefront of Android developments, the Pixel is also a leader when it comes to bugs. The latest has arrived with September’s Android 17 QPR1 release . Pixel owners are registering an issue they’re having with incorrect animations on the home and recent apps screens ever since the update. Over on Reddit’s Pixel sub, our original poster shares that when they try to return to the launcher from an app on their Pixel 10 Pro XL, instead of the downward animation they previously would get, the app goes to the recent apps screen and then slides away to the right. Additionally, they note that when they go to the recent apps screen from within an app, the app icon sometimes gets stuck on the screen while the recent apps screen opens behind it.

title: Survey reveals Kindle readers aren’t buying Amazon’s pricey page-turning solution
summary: Amazon's new Kindle Page-Turn Cover promises extra convenience, but our readers have strong opinions about the price tag.
body: Credit: Amazon Physical page-turn buttons might seem like a pretty basic feature for an e-reader , but Amazon has spent years leaving them off its Kindle lineup. The company has given bookworms a way to bring them back with its latest devices, although it’s charging a hefty premium for the privilege. We recently asked readers whether they’d be willing to pay $80 for this convenience, and the results suggest Amazon might have misread the room. As my colleague Dhruv Bhutani explained in his recent look at the 2026 Kindle refresh , Amazon’s new Page-Turn Cover adds physical buttons to the e-reader through a magnetic connection. The catch is that it costs $80 and it only works with the Signature Editions of the Kindle Paperwhite and Colorsoft, which already cost $250 and $320, respectively. That makes $330 the minimum entry price if you want physical buttons on a new Kindle. We wanted to know whether you thought this was fair enough, or if perhaps Amazon should have just included this functionality as part of the deal.
